articleTitle: Next-Generation Protocols for Enhanced Connectivity in Heterogeneous IoT
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: The rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has engendered a complex and diverse ecosystem, demanding innovative solutions to ensure seamless connectivity. This research introduces a novel "Next-Generation Protocols for Enhanced Connectivity in Heterogeneous IoT Ecosystems" method, which addresses the critical challenges posed by this heterogeneity, scalability, security, and energy efficiency. This method leverages adaptability, advanced encryption, and energy-efficient communication mechanisms. The proposed methodology comprises three key algorithms. The Scalability-Optimized Routing Algorithm dynamically adapts routing paths, optimizing data transmission. The Secure Data Exchange Algorithm ensures data integrity and privacy through advanced encryption. The Energy-Efficient Communication Algorithm enhances the longevity of battery-powered IoT devices. Comparative performance evaluations with six original methods, including Lightweight M2M (LwM2M), CoAP, 6LoWPAN, MQTT, DDS, and Zigbee, clearly demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method across security, scalability, reliability, and energy efficiency parameters. This innovative approach paves the way for a more connected, secure, energy-efficient, and adaptive IoT ecosystem.

articleTitle: Traffic Flow Optimizer: Traffic Signal Control With Vehicle Density and Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: The goal of this work is to create an intelligent traffic signal control system that will enhance intersection traffic flow. The major goals are to reduce traffic congestion, expedite travel, and improve all-around road safety. To estimate traffic density in real time, the system uses image processing methods, specifically vehicle detection algorithms. The computer vision library is used to evaluate surveillance camera footage at traffic lights in order to precisely count vehicles and gauge traffic density. To detect vehicles and precisely count them, a variety of image processing techniques are applied, such as object recognition and background subtraction. The number of vehicles per area or lane is then taken into account when calculating traffic density. A central server receives this data for further processing.

articleTitle: Sarcasm Detection in News Headlines Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: A communication technique known as sarcasm is used to express an emotion that is opposite or distinct from the literal meaning of the words being used, typically for satire, criticism, or amusement. Sarcasm detection is the process of identifying language that purposefully conveys the opposite meaning of what is being said. Today's sarcasm detection techniques employ a range of deep learning (DL) and machine learning (ML) algorithms, including logistic regression, random forests, decision trees, long short-term memories (LSTM), convolution neural networks (CNN) etc. However, these methods have limitations in accurately detecting sarcasm, particularly when dealing with large datasets. In this paper, we aim to provide a better method for sarcasm identification in news headlines that combines LSTM and CNN algorithms enhancing sarcasm detection's accuracy and here we managed to achieve nearly greater than 97% of accuracy by leveraging the strengths of both algorithms. Using a dataset of news headlines, we have also compared our hybrid model to other models to see how effective our proposed approach is more accurate.

articleTitle: Automated Detection of Potato Plant Diseases using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: The agriculture industry is a crucial sector globally and plays a vital role in providing food, raw materials, and employment opportunities. However, the industry is faced with various challenges such as climate change, water scarcity, and plant diseases. Plant diseases, in particular, can cause significant damages to crop yield and quality, affecting food security and leading to economic losses. This research paper proposes an automated disease detection system for potato plants using five different machine learning algorithms, including KNN, Random Forest, CNN, Naive Bayes, and SVM and chooses the most accurate model. The system analyzes images of plant leaves to accurately classify them as healthy or diseased and even identify the specific disease affecting the plant and display results in a website. The proposed approach has the potential to provide a reliable and efficient solution for disease detection in potato plants providing higher accuracy than the previous studies in this field. it can help farmers make informed decisions and take timely action to control the spread of diseases, ultimately contributing to improving food security and the overall sustainability of the agriculture industry.

articleTitle: Breaking the Boundaries of Oncological Diagnosis: A Holistic Framework for Multi-Cancer Identification and Comprehensive Diagnostic Reporting Utilizing Advanced AI and NLP
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: Innovative deep learning models for cancer classification, including VGG-19, DenseNet201, MobileNetV3, ResNet50V2, YOLOv5, and GPT-2, have completely changed the way that doctors diagnose cancer. This study introduces a multi-modal technique for an accurate and speedy cancer diagnosis. With the aid of cutting-edge technology, this system combines object identification (YOLOv5), natural language processing (GPT-2), and picture classification models (VGG-19, DenseNet201, MobileNetV3, ResNet50V2) to provide scientists and medical professionals with a flexible toolkit. It generates thorough reports with tumour images and spots malignant irregularities. Diagnostic accuracy is improved by real-time application, which benefits laboratories by reducing turnaround times and medical practitioners by providing an important decision support tool. Reports with tumour photos enhance the capacity to comprehend results. This study is important because it has the potential to improve cancer detection by using cutting-edge algorithms and models. This research also promises to improve patient care, prediction, and therapy. The practical method presented in this paper ushers in a new age in medical diagnostics by empowering laboratories and doctors.

articleTitle: Predictive Analysis of Daily Activities on A Mobile Device using Shallow CNN
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: An emerging area of artificial intelligence and machine learning called "Human Activity Recognition" (HAR) aims to create systems that can comprehend and categorize human movements and behaviors. HAR uses data captured from wearable devices, smartphones, and other sensors to infer activities performed by individuals. Leveraging sophisticated machine learning algorithms, HAR systems are capable of accurately identifying a wide variety of actions, from straightforward gestures to challenging physical demands. But a major obstacle to HAR’s current state is the lack of detailed data on how much time is spent sitting, standing, lying down, and being active. Existing wearable devices and health trackers primarily focus on providing inactivity alerts, leaving users with incomplete insights into their overall activity patterns and posture distribution throughout the day. This information gap hinders users’ ability to monitor and improve their sedentary behaviors, leading to potential health risks and suboptimal activity management. Reciprocating this challenge, the proposed solution aims to utilize motion sensor data from gyroscopes and accelerometers found in smartphones to determine position of a human using a Shallow Convolution Neural Network (SCNN) model.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning-Based Tomato Disease Prediction using Leaf Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: Tomato plants are among the most important of all the fundamental crops, valued highly by both farmers and consumers. The biggest concern for tomato farmers is that the plant is becoming infected with unidentified diseases. Farmers must recognize the type of disease to treat the plants appropriately when numerous diseases could hinder growth. The goal of this project is to create three distinct transfer learning models that can accurately identify the type of sickness. The most effective algorithm for this purpose is also finalized. For this purpose, a dataset of more than 10,000 images is collected from Kaggle. This collection contains pictures of tomato plant leaves in both a healthy and a diseased state. Three sorts of data must be created: training, testing, and validation. The smallest portion is utilized to validate the model, while the second largest portion is used to test the model for its final parameters. After separating, the photographs are preprocessed. In this study, image scaling is the only preprocessing technique used. The transfer learning models that were developed utilizing three different transfer learning strategies are then tested and trained using the preprocessed and divided images. In this experiment, the VGG-16, AlexNet, and hybrid algorithms were applied. Testing, validation, and training outcomes are recorded. But next, to enhance readability and facilitate analysis, the data is converted by being plotted onto a graph. Throughout the training, the hybrid model showed significantly greater performance than the other two models. The models created using the VGG-16 and AlexNet algorithms displayed a lot of oscillations, even when the margin shrank during validation, which could lead to inconsistent performance. The model can be used in the future to help farmers and other agriculturists accurately identify a problem with their plant and search for a workable remedy by integrating it into the backend processor of a website or software application uses pre-trained convolutional weights to optimize the model.

articleTitle: Quantum Computing Enhancements in Deep Learning Models for Cybersecurity
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: The cybersecurity industry has undergone a sea change due to the combination of quantum computing and deep learning models. This study presents a novel approach that makes use of the unique features of quantum computing to improve the efficiency and safety of deep learning models used in cybersecurity. The suggested method improves upon previous methods in terms of both the precision and efficiency with which threats may be identified and categorized by making use of Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs), Quantum Support Vector Machines (QSVMs), and Quantum Key Distribution (QKD). Our findings show that the suggested method is superior to conventional approaches through a thorough examination of detection accuracy and computing efficiency. Combining quantum computing principles with deep learning techniques provides a game-changing answer to the growing complexity of today's cybersecurity threats.

articleTitle: Bridging Diverse Business Domains through Optimized Digital Platforms in Industrial Syndicates
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: In an era characterized by rapid technological advancements and volatile business environments, synergy across numerous business sectors within industrial syndicates has emerged as a major issue and opportunity. There is no way to ignore this challenge and opportunity. The optimization of digital platforms to span a variety of different fields gives a thorough analysis of the potentially disruptive possibilities. The intention is to promote cooperation among participants in industrial syndicates, improve the distribution of available resources, and spark creative thinking. The method that has been presented makes use of cutting-edge technology to create a dynamic ecosystem where many businesses can interact with one another and share knowledge invisibly. This technology includes artificial intelligence, machine learning, blockchain, and the Internet of Things. In this study, a strategic road map is constructed using evolutionary algorithms, reinforcement learning, and clustering approaches to improve resource allocation, decision-making processes, and information sharing. The route map was constructed using these methods. These tactics aim to achieve the highest levels of productivity, adaptability, and teamwork, which will ultimately usher industrial syndicates into a new era of competitiveness. This essay examines many real-world case studies in depth and focuses on how these benefits might be realized to show the practical advantages of adopting an optimal digital platform paradigm. These case studies demonstrate how distinct organizations, which were previously divided due to antiquated practices, may make advantage of the potential of multidisciplinary collaboration to confront challenging global issues. The study also makes suggestions for a culture change inside industrial syndicates, one that promotes collaboration, fosters creativity, and acknowledges the potential for new technology to upend society. If industrial syndicates promote an innovation culture that cuts across different domains and embraces digital

articleTitle: Enhancing Medical Image Recognition through Automated Neural Network Architecture Optimization using Neuroevolvenet
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: Medical image recognition is pivotal for accurate diagnostics and treatment planning. Traditional neural network architecture design methods are often time-consuming and suboptimal. To address this, an automated framework, NeuroEvolveNet is proposed for optimizing neural network architectures in medical image recognition. NeuroEvolveNet effectively investigates alternative architectural configurations for improved recognition accuracy by utilizing evolutionary algorithms. The difficulties of manual architectural design in medical imaging and the evolutionary strategy used by NeuroEvolveNet are outlined here. Our method is tailored for medical imaging data and is evaluated on a diverse medical image dataset. Through comprehensive experiments and various metrics, including accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, the framework's effectiveness is demonstrated. Results consistently showcase NeuroEvolveNet's superiority over manual designs and existing methods. Evolved architectures exhibit higher accuracy, illustrating the potential of automated optimization in medical image recognition. Our study emphasizes benefits such as customization, efficiency, and adaptability in complex medical imaging tasks.This research contributes a novel method at the intersection of machine learning and healthcare, addressing challenges in medical image recognition. The integration of automated architecture optimization, as demonstrated by NeuroEvolveNet, holds promise for enhancing diagnostic accuracy and patient care in healthcare applications.

articleTitle: The Convergence of Modern Digital Solutions with Online Retail Offers a Comprehensive Examination from Seller and Buyer Standpoints
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: The convergence of modern digital solutions with online retail has ushered in a transformative era for both sellers and buyers. In this research, we present a comprehensive examination of this convergence from the perspectives of sellers and buyers. Our study encompasses the development of a novel proposed method, which is compared with several traditional methods, to assess the impact on various facets of online retail. The research explores multiple dimensions, including inventory management, marketing strategies, customer satisfaction, conversion rates, return rates, data security, sales revenue, and personalization effectiveness. The proposed method leverages the power of data-driven analysis and machine learning to provide enhanced insights and decision-making capabilities for online retailers. We evaluate its performance against traditional methods in these diverse aspects, seeking to determine whether modern digital solutions can indeed offer a competitive edge in the everevolving online retail landscape. Our findings reveal that the proposed method consistently outperforms traditional methods in several critical metrics. It demonstrates higher accuracy, precision, and recall, indicating its superior predictive power. Additionally, the proposed method exhibits a lower execution time, highlighting its efficiency in processing and analysis. Scalability, too, is a strong suit, making it suitable for handling larger datasets and accommodating the growing needs of online retail. In conclusion, the convergence of modern digital solutions with online retail is a game-changer for the industry, providing an opportunity for sellers to enhance their strategies and for buyers to enjoy a more personalized and satisfying shopping experience. The proposed method is the shining star in this transformation, showcasing better performance across various evaluation criteria. As the digital retail landscape continues to evolve, embracing modern solutions is not just a choice; it is the way forward for online retailers who seek to excel in the market.

articleTitle: Exploring Agartha: A Subterranean Odyssey
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: In-depth study on successful open-world games, examination of user behavior and preferences, and ongoing incorporation of user feedback throughout the production process are all necessary to create an immersive open-world game. With a compelling and cogent storyline maintained, the planned game "Agartha" attempts to give players an experience of limitless exploration. This paper explores the exciting world of open-world role-playing games (RPGs), which are propelled by the modern Unreal Engine 5. The paper explores the incredible levels of immersion and involvement possible in this genre with an emphasis on the most recent developments in game creation technology. This article demonstrates the possibility for building vast virtual worlds where players may easily explore, interact with the environment, and connect with in-game creatures in a way that exceeds traditional gaming experiences by utilizing Unreal Engine 5's powerful capabilities. This study provides light on the revolutionary influence of Unreal Engine 5 in influencing the future of open-world RPGs through a thorough investigation of game mechanics, graphical fidelity, and player agency. Excellent visuals and more functionality than an earlier version of Unreal Engine was offered by Unreal Engine 5. The findings of this investigation open the door to a new era of gaming experiences characterized by unparalleled depth and realism.

articleTitle: Unraveling the Mysteries of Mind-Wandering and Meditation: A Comprehensive Investigation using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: Mind-wandering and meditation are two intriguing cognitive states that have captivated researchers across various disciplines for their profound implications on human consciousness and mental well-being. Mind-wandering refers to the involuntary drifting of thoughts away from the present task, while meditation aims to cultivate focused attention and mindfulness. Traditional research methodologies have provided valuable insights into these phenomena, but their subjective nature and limited scalability call for innovative approaches. This paper presents a pioneering investigation that leverages the power of deep learning, specifically Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), to explore the differences in mind-wandering patterns between novices and meditators. This study is guided by the compilation of a comprehensive dataset incorporating cognitive and neural measures related to mind-wandering and meditation, providing a novel perspective on the impact of meditation on mind-wandering.

articleTitle: Pioneering Approaches for Accurate Vocal Anomaly Detection using State-of-the-Art Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: Accurate Vocal Anomaly Detection (AVAD) has emerged as a critical area of research with far-reaching implications for healthcare, security, and human-computer interaction. This paper presents pioneering approaches for AVAD using state-of-the-art machine learning models. Leveraging the power of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and Support Vector Machines (SVMs), our proposed method demonstrates remarkable efficacy in identifying vocal anomalies indicative of various health conditions and security threats. In the data preprocessing phase, we extract Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) as vocal features, providing a robust foundation for subsequent analysis. The CNN, adept at capturing local patterns and hierarchies in feature maps, showcases impressive performance in classifying vocal data. LSTMs, renowned for capturing temporal dependencies in sequential data, enhance the model's ability to detect anomalies within vocal patterns. SVMs, with their capacity to construct optimal hyperplanes in feature space, serve as an additional valuable tool for accurate anomaly detection. Our comprehensive evaluation incorporates a range of performance metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, ROC-AUC, sensitivity, and specificity. The results demonstrate that our proposed method excels in accurately detecting vocal anomalies across diverse use cases, opening doors to early diagnosis, healthcare monitoring, and enhanced security measures through vocal analysis.

articleTitle: Analysis of User Behavior Patterns using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: A weblog is a dynamic record of transactions regularly updated by website visitors. It contains a variety of information, such as IP addresses, status codes, bytes sent, categories, and timestamps. The primary purpose of a weblog is to monitor user behavior and classify their interests based on different categories and qualities. This study aims to achieve two main objectives: first, to categorize successful responses, and second, to distinguish between normal and abnormal user behavior. The research process outlined in this paper involves several steps. It begins with data collection, where relevant information is gathered from the weblogs. The next step is data pre-processing, which involves cleaning and organizing the data to make it suitable for analysis. The researchers then employ clustering techniques to identify different patterns of user activity, enabling a quick assessment and prediction of user behavior. The main focus of the research is user prediction, achieved by analyzing user preferences extracted from the weblogs at various levels. To accomplish this, the researchers utilize various machine learning techniques. One of the implemented models is the Random Forest Classifier, which is utilized to predict user behavior based on specific input parameters.

articleTitle: NeuroPredict: A Comprehensive Approach for Alzheimer’s Disease Prediction and Development of a Medical Assisting Kit
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: The "NeuroPredict" system aims to address Alzheimer’s disease (AD) by providing early prediction and diagnosis using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model on MRI images. With an 80% accuracy rate, the proposed NeuroPredict system offers a robust solution. Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) is emphasized to uncover patterns and trends within the AD dataset, contributing to research advancements. Additionally, the system introduces "MemorEyes," a low-cost hardware kit to assist AD individuals. Smart spectacles display pictures of loved ones with details, reminders for exercise and medication, and a smart wristband for live location tracking. Caretakers receive alerts, promoting proactive prevention and personalized support for early-stage AD patients. To ensure accessibility, NeuroPredict offers a user-friendly web application for clinicians and researchers. The user can easily upload MRI images, run predictions using the CNN model, and access detailed reports and visualizations, even without technical expertise. The proposed NeuroPredict focuses on early prediction, proactive prevention, and personalized care and aims to significantly impact AD patients’ lives and help in neurodegenerative disease research.

articleTitle: Generative Adversarial Networks for Cybersecurity Threat
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: We provide a unique method to enhance cybersecurity threat prediction using generative adversarial networks (GANs). Through competitive training, the generator and discriminator parts of GANs are customized for application in the cybersecurity industry. Three key algorithms underlie this method. First, to create believable threats, GANs are employed in the GAN Architecture for Threat Generation. The discriminator distinguishes between actual and phony threat data, while the generator generates false threat data. These simulated assaults are a significant part of cybersecurity threat predictions. Second, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks are used in the Threat Scenario Prediction Algorithm's Time Series Forecasting Algorithm. To predict possible outcomes, long short-term memory (LSTM) models the temporal dependency of historical threat data. This approach offers perceptions into prospective threats, enabling the adoption of preventative actions. Finally, Markov chains are used by the Threat Evolution Algorithm to depict the dynamic evolution of cybersecurity threats. In order to shed light on how dangers vary over time, it forecasts the chance of a transition from one state of hazard to another. We get a deeper understanding of threat trajectories and how they influence an organization's cybersecurity by adopting a more dynamic approach. This comprehensive approach combines state-of-the-art techniques in threat scenario generation, forecasting, and evolution modeling, providing organizations with a robust toolset to proactively address cybersecurity challenges.

articleTitle: Empowering Communication: Harnessing CNN and Mediapipe for Sign Language Interpretation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: Sign language serves as a crucial communication medium for the Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing community. However, the lack of automated systems for sign language recognition can limit interaction with people who are unfamiliar with it. This study proposes a real-time sign language detection system leveraging OpenCV for image preprocessing, MediaPipe for hand tracking, and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for gesture classification. The system captures video feed, isolates hand regions, and identifies gestures that correspond to alphabets in American Sign Language (ASL). Through this model, it has achieved a promising classification accuracy, thereby showing significant promise for real-world applications. This work aims to bridge the communication gap by facilitating seamless interaction between hearing impaired individuals and the broader community, enhancing inclusivity and accessibility.

articleTitle: Covid-19 Detection using X-Ray Images and Fake X-Ray Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: The infectious disease COVID-19 has propagated around the Globe in 2019, including to Indonesia. Due to the lack of a vaccine to either treat or stop the spread of the virus, this worldwide pandemic turns into a deadly epidemic. Given that the Rapid Test is more affordable than the SWAB test, it is chosen as the primary method for finding Covid-19 in Indonesia. The hospital's Covid-19 test has a limited capacity due to the rise in Covid-19 patients, thus the newest technology is required to identify and treat this pandemic problem. Thus, the objective of the current study is to evaluate more than hundred X-ray chest images of Covid-19 patients and more than hundred X-ray chest images of healthy individuals. Nowadays, fraudulent photos are widely disseminated through digital media. The exposure of image-based cybercrimes requires the discovery of such phony pictures. In this digital world, research on forging photos and spotting them has promise. By employing a neural network to identify the areas of the picture that have been altered and to show the portions of the original image, the tampered photos are identified. It may be used on the Android platform and afterwards made available to regular users. By applying error level analysis, it is possible to identify the foreign material in a phony picture by comparing its compression ratio to that of the real image. Image metadata is a characteristic that is utilized in conjunction with compression ratio. Although it is possible to modify metadata content to make it unreliable on its own, it is used here as a supporting parameter for the ELA decision.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning in Automated Network Vulnerability Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: In today's rapidly changing digital environment, identifying security holes in a network is an essential part of maintaining online safety. This research suggests a novel strategy for improving automated network vulnerability identification by making use of Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). Our approach combines cutting-edge algorithms to provide a versatile and responsive system; these algorithms include Deep Q-Network (DQN), Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), and Dueling Deep Q-Network (DDQN). Using six different methods—including signature-based detection, heuristic-based detection, machine learning-based detection, intrusion detection systems (IDS), packet sniffers, and vulnerability scanners—we evaluate how well the suggested method performs in comparison. The detection rate, the number of false positives and negatives, the precision, the recall, the speed of execution, and the capacity to scale are only few of the major performance parameters we use in our analysis. Across a variety of metrics, the results show that the suggested approach performs better than the state of the art. It has an incredibly low false positive (3%) and false negative (2%) rates on top of its 95% detection accuracy. Both its accuracy and efficiency in finding security flaws are demonstrated by its high precision (94%) and recall (96%). The suggested technique also has a low execution time of 25 ms and a good scalability rating of 5, showing it can scale to deal with increasing network complexity. In conclusion, our study demonstrates the use of DRL in automating the process of detecting security holes in networks. The suggested method is an excellent tool for improving network security since it is more accurate and efficient than conventional methods and can be adapted to deal with new threats. By incorporating sophisticated DRL algorithms, a resilient and flexible defensive system may be created, one that can keep up with the ever-changing threats in the cyber world.

articleTitle: The Role of Modern Machine Intelligence in Decoding Activity Patterns from Visual Data of Various Organisms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: The integration of modern machine intelligence presents a transformative paradigm in the study of organisms' behaviors through visual data analysis. Leveraging deep learning algorithms like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), this approach automates the extraction of intricate patterns from images and videos, enabling comprehensive insights into diverse organisms. Object detection algorithms further facilitate precise tracking. By surpassing traditional methods, it enhances accuracy and scalability. Ethical considerations guide responsible research. This fusion of technology and ecology fosters a deeper understanding of natural ecosystems, paving the way for sustainable coexistence with the environment and the preservation of biodiversity.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Visual Question Answering model for the Visually Impaired
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: There is a need for diagnostic tests to assess our progress and identify issues involved in constructing deep learning systems that can reason and respond to queries regarding visual input. The requirement to gain feature descriptions of the images that are present on the Web presents a difficulty for those who are visually impaired. Visual Question Answering aims to respond to the questions of the blind. Visual Question Answering is the study of machines which learn from input data in the form of images to extract features and provide answers to the posed questions by the user. Existing standards for answering questions visually can be useful, but they contain strong bias that models can use to answer the given questions accurately without using logic. Additionally, the models combine several inputs of inaccuracy, making it challenging to identify model flaws. In general, the VQA used in this project is an algorithm that takes input as an image along with a human understandable language question and it produces natural language answers as its output. VQA is a multi-disciplinary research problem by nature. The model uses a dataset that assesses many aspects of visual reasoning. It has few biases and extensive annotations that describe the type of reasoning that each question necessitates. After this, analysis of various contemporary visual reasoning systems such as LSTM Q+I, EQ-1, and ALMA which utilize multiple approaches to solving questions but are subject to overtraining and making answer prediction complex. To keep things simple, the model will be utilizing CNN and LSTM which is using VQA-2.0 dataset, offering fresh perspectives on their strengths and weaknesses. With the huge potential of VQA, the readers can see that it is a necessity for further research to take place.

articleTitle: Live Tracking of Metro Rail using Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: The Live Tracking System for Metro Rail using IoT is a proposed project that aims to provide real-time location tracking of Metro trains to passengers and authorities. The project utilizes IoT devices and wireless communication tech- nologies to collect and transmit data about the current location of the train. The system consists of a GPS sensor, microcontroller, and wireless communication modules installed on each train. The GPS sensors collect the current location of the train, which is then processed by the microcontroller to determine the train’s speed and direction. The wireless communication module transmits this data to a central server, which processes the data and presents it to passengers and authorities in real-time. The proposed system will have a user-friendly interface accessible through a mobile application, web portal, or kiosk. Passengers will be able to view real-time information about the train’s location, estimated arrival and departure time, and any delays or disruptions on the route. The system will also provide Metro corporation authorities with valuable insights into train operations, enabling them to improve service quality and enhance safety measures.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Battery Management System Equalization Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: Electric batteries are being used more frequently as a result of the growing adoption of electric vehicles (EVs). To get the high voltage needed by EVs, battery packs are created by joining several battery cells together. A battery pack’s linked battery cells should ideally all have the same voltage. However, achieving perfect voltage uniformity across the cells is difficult in practise because of a number of inescapable circumstances. EVs and other battery-powered gadgets have considerable challenges while operating safely and effectively due to unbalanced battery cell voltages. Reduced storage capabilities and, in severe situations, explosions or fires, can be brought about by these voltage imbalances. As a result, the equalisation of battery cell voltages has grown to be a crucial area of research, with the goal of creating and improving methods that deal with this problem. Incorporating different significant features, numerous studies have been done to investigate and enhance battery cell voltage equalisation techniques. This study offers a thorough and methodical analysis of several cell equalisation methods. An inductor-based, SC-based, and resistor-based equalisation circuit case study is used to compare the performance of the two equalisation circuits.

articleTitle: Multivariate Fast Iterative Filtering Algorithm for Denoising of Ocular Artifacts in EEG
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: The elimination of artifacts including ocular movements in multichannel long-standing scalp EEG recordings has been the goal of extensive research with the aim to distinguish epileptic seizure episodes in EEG signals. The current research introduces a method for effectively eliminating ocular artifacts (OA) from extended EEG recordings by employing multivariate fast iterative filtering (MVFIF) in conjunction with a total variation (TV) denoising technique. The current approach initially employs the MVFIF for signal decomposition and then filters the selected noisy IMFs with a TV denoising scheme. The evaluation of the denoising impact involves mean absolute error (MAE), the power spectral density distortion (PSDD), and mutual information (MI) metrics. Applied to actual EEG data, the proposed methodology successfully eliminates OA components and yields a minimal MAE of 0.0020.

articleTitle: A Multimodal Approach Utilizing the IOMT to Address both the Pandemic and its Aftermath
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: Many IOT in the healthcare industry offers improved medical facilities for patients, benefiting doctors' offices and hospitals as well. The Internet of Medical Things (IOMT) plays a crucial role in enhancing the accuracy, reliability, and efficiency of electronic devices within the healthcare sector. Researchers are advancing a digital healthcare system by connecting existing medical resources and healthcare services. While IOT is impacting various industries, our focus is on its research contributions to the healthcare sector. The proposed system integrates multiple medical equipment, such as sensors and web or mobile-based applications, enabling communication across a network. This system facilitates the monitoring and storage of patient health data and medical information during the pandemic situation and after math. Additionally, using machine learning and data analysis, the proposed system aids in predicting the severity of the pandemic in different zones, offering potential solutions. The system seeks to improve outcomes for post-COVID-19 patients by using a multimodal approach to track their health.

articleTitle: The Rise of Advanced Computational Techniques for Holistic Analysis of Human Gaze Behavior and Its Significance
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: The Rise of Advanced Computational Techniques for Holistic Analysis of Human Gaze Behavior and Its Significance Gaze behavior analysis has emerged as a crucial area of study with broad implications for psychology, neuroscience, human-computer interaction, and more. In this research, we introduce an innovative methodology that leverages advanced computational techniques to provide a holistic analysis of human gaze behavior. Our proposed method, GazeNet, combines Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), and Gaussian Mixture Models (GMMs) to capture both temporal and spatial aspects of gaze data. GazeNet excels in predictive modeling, enabling real-time applications in diverse fields. In this study, we compare the performance of GazeNet with ten original methods, including Visual Gaze Analysis, Eye-Tracking Analytics, and Gaze Behavior Pattern Recognition. The comparison includes accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score, revealing that GazeNet consistently outperforms its counterparts. Furthermore, GazeNet provides comprehensive insights into cognitive processes, surpassing traditional methods. Our research signifies the transformative potential of GazeNet in psychology, neuroscience, clinical diagnostics, and real-world applications like user experience design and driver safety. The integration of advanced computational techniques brings a new level of precision and efficiency to gaze analysis, enabling a deeper understanding of human attention allocation.

articleTitle: Harnessing Advanced Computational Techniques for Efficient Handling of Nanoscale Thermal Analysis Instruments via Flexible Architectures
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: The abstract for "Harnessing Advanced Computational Techniques for Efficient Handling of Nanoscale Thermal Analysis Instruments via Flexible Architectures" summarizes a study focused on optimizing the use of nanoscale thermal analysis instruments through advanced computational methods and flexible architectures. The research aims to enhance the efficiency of these instruments by leveraging computational techniques, enabling more precise and controlled thermal analysis at the nanoscale. The study's findings hold promise for applications in various fields, including materials science and nanotechnology, by improving our ability to analyze and manipulate thermal properties at extremely small scales.

articleTitle: An Approach for Ranking Cyber Crime using Fuzzy AHP and Fuzzy TOPSIS
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: Cybercrime is a major obstacle in both the IT community and the law community. In this paper, we are trying to rank different types of cybercrime using Fuzzy AHP and Fuzzy TOPSIS. Not all types of cybercrime cause financial loss to an individual. In this paper, we have considered eleven different types of cybercrime all these criteria were selected on the basis of the extent of financial losses incurred upon a person. We have used Fuzzy AHP to rank the criteria and Fuzzy TOPSIS was mainly used to see whether there were any financial incurred by a person. The main aim of this paper is to rank the criteria that can help in future research in cybercrime

articleTitle: Advanced Neural Network Models for Predictive Analytics and Healthcare Management in Neurodegenerative Diseases
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: Our proposed method, HybridNet-NDM, leverages three critical algorithms - Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs), synergistically applied to predictive analytics and healthcare management for neurodegenerative diseases. CNNs are employed to extract biomarkers from medical imaging data, capturing intricate patterns critical for neurodegenerative disease identification. LSTMs model temporal aspects of patient data, aiding in disease progression prediction using longitudinal records. GCNs analyze brain connectivity patterns, providing insights into disease development based on brain structure and function. The hybrid neural network combines these algorithms, integrating their respective features to achieve superior predictive power. An attention mechanism further refines the feature fusion, enabling precise predictions. Our optimized model demonstrates enhanced performance across various metrics, showcasing its effectiveness in predictive analytics and healthcare management for neurodegenerative diseases.

articleTitle: Decoding Digits: Advancements in hand written Digit Recognition with Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: One of the most challenging besides fascinating fields of image processing and pattern recognition has been the recognition of handwritten characters and numbers. This paper's primary goal is to illustrate and reflect the work that has been done in the area of hand-written digit recognition. areas of pattern recognition and image processing is a highly challenging task. It is difficult to extract features from and segment handwritten numerical script because the numbers in this identification challenge are not precisely written or scripted since they vary in size or shape. In the suggested work, segmentation is accomplished by the use of vertical and horizontal projections. Convex envelope technique is used for feature extraction, whereas SVM is employed in recognition and and classification.

Author Keywords: Text Extraction and Analysis naive Bayesian Classifier

articleTitle: Seismic Signal Processing and Aftershock Analysis using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: The anticipated method aims to develop a robust machine learning-based approach for aftershock classification using seismic sensing signals. Accurate classification of after- shocks plays a crucial role in understanding seismic processes and assessing risks associated with earthquakes. By distinguishing aftershocks from mainshocks and background noise, we enhance earthquake hazard prediction and mitigation. proposed methodology combines feature extraction techniques, machine learning algorithms, and rigorous evaluation measures for reliable aftershock classification. The study begins with an introduction to aftershock classification’s significance in earthquake research and disaster management, followed by a literature survey exploring existing methodologies and their limitations. Machine learning algorithms are identified as promising solutions for these challenges, motivating the choice of methodology. We preprocess seismic sensing signals through data cleaning and noise reduction to ensure high-quality input. Feature extraction methods capture signal characteristics, including statistical, time- domain, and spectral features. These extracted features serve as input to the primary classification algorithm, the SVM, which is best suited to handle complex data and non linear relationships with ease and effectiveness. SVM is trained on a labeled dataset comprising manually classified aftershocks and other seismic events, with hyperparameter tuning for optimization Extensive experiments on a specific region’s seismic dataset demonstrate outstanding accuracy, with an F1-score of 0.99974 and 99.98% accuracy. High precision and recall values indicate reliable aftershock classification, as confirmed by negligible false positives and false negatives from the confusion matrix analysis. In conclusion, this research presents a robust machine learning- based approach for aftershock classification using seismic sensing signals. The methodology offers high accuracy and reliability, contributing to earthquake research and disaster management by enabling precise aftershock identification. It is extendable to various seismic datasets and applicable in real-time earthquake monitoring systems. Future work involves exploring additional machine learning algorithms, incorporating domain knowledge, and integrating the models into operational systems to support seismic event decision-making

articleTitle: Study on VGG16 Transfer learning Model for Goat/Sheep Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: The utilization of deep learning and transfer learning methodologies in the realm of image classification has resulted in notable progress across diverse domains. This research paper presents an analysis of the performance of VGG16 model when incorporating transfer learning techniques in conjunction with various regularization techniques for the purpose of image classification of goat and sheep images. By employing the technique of transfer learning, we have successfully fine-tuned the VGG16 models on a dataset comprising six distinct classes of goats and sheep. This process has enabled the models to adapt their pre-existing features, which were initially trained on a different task, to the specific requirements of our target task. Performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, and recall rate are employed in the evaluation of a model's capabilities. Although each strategy had its own distinct advantages, the strategies that consistently yielded balanced precision, recall, F1-scores, and accuracy were a dropout rate of 0.5 and L2 regularization. Whereas L2 Regularization outperformed the other models with a testing accuracy of 0.839.

articleTitle: Analysis of Mental and Physical Health for Personality Development using Fuzzy AHP and Fuzzy Topsis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: The complex interactions between mental and physical health highlight the demand for a thorough and accurate method of health analysis. In order to provide a solid framework for assessing both mental and physical health indices, this study introduces a thorough technique that integrates the Fuzzy Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (Fuzzy TOPSIS) and Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (Fuzzy AHP). This study gives a new perspective on the use of fuzzy TOPSIS in the area of health evaluation in order to provide a comprehensive framework for evaluating both mental and physical health aspects. Fuzzy TOPSIS and Fuzzy AHP used together to examine physical and mental well-being give a complete picture of a person's overall wellbeing. By including both physical and mental well-being difficulties, this method provides a full understanding of health status and its dynamic nature, underlining the importance of treating both dimensions in healthcare planning. This paper provides an overview of the key components of the technique, including data preparation, criterion weighting, and decision-making procedures. In order to rank the elements, we are taking into consideration criteria in this study that are based on both MH and PH. This method holds the potential to enhance healthcare decision-making, leading to more effective healthcare interventions and improved overall health outcomes by providing a flexible and comprehensive framework for evaluating and prioritizing both mental and physical health criteria.

articleTitle: Leveraging Deep Learning Techniques for Profiling and Categorizing Lung and Pancreatic Tumors
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: The study provides a unique strategy for "Leveraging Deep Learning Techniques for Profiling and Categorizing Lung and Pancreatic Tumors." The suggested technique incorporates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for image analysis, Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) for temporal modeling, and Transfer Learning to fine-tune pre-trained models. It aims to improve tumor classification precision by tackling the particular challenges given by pancreatic and lung cancers. The outcomes of our investigation show that the proposed strategy outperforms existing methods in numerous key areas. F1 was 0.85, specificity was 0.87, recall was 0.82, accuracy was 0.85, precision was 0.88, and area under the curve was 0.92, according to the results. These values routinely exceed six original conventional approaches, including CNNs, RNNs, Transfer Learning, Autoencoders, Support Vector Machines (SVMs), and Reinforcement Learning. The confusion matrix measurements further underscore the superiority of the suggested strategy with more true positives and true negatives, and fewer false positives and false negatives. In conclusion, the suggested strategy improves the accuracy and objectivity of lung and pancreatic tumor profiling by harnessing the power of deep learning and a multi-faceted approach. It offers a more tailored, efficient, and data-driven approach to the arduous issue of tumor classification. The data clearly illustrate its superiority over traditional approaches, making it a potential innovation in the field of cancer.

articleTitle: Secondary Prevention of Acute Coronary Syndrome Using Data Science Analysis and Profile Representation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: Coronary vein sickness (computer aided design) is brought about by atherosclerosis in the coronary courses and prompts heart failure and coronary failure. CAD is diagnosed through the highly technical, time-consuming, and expensive angiography procedure. In order to diagnose and quantify the severity of cardiac disease, researchers are looking for alternative methods, such as machine learning algorithms. The prediction accuracy of the decision tree, which is 99.5%, is the highest. Additionally, we evaluated our strategy against a benchmarked set of heart disease data. In this scenario, MLR outperforms other strategies as well. In recent years, increased focus has been placed on the Comparison of enormous volumes of data from electronic medical records (EMRs) and regular clinical practise data sources. Even so, only a few number of organised techniques were created to assist in the extraction of the abundance and variety of data across different sources of information. Because of its high mortality and morbidity rates, acute coronary syndrome (ACS) statistics can be found in a lot of medical facilities.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Performance of Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models in Detecting Cyberbullying Comments
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: With the proliferation of social media platforms, there has been a concerning escalation in cyberbullying and abusive language. Detecting such toxic comments in large volumes of user-generated data presents challenges. This research conducts a comparative analysis to evaluate the impact of natural language processing techniques on identifying cyberbullying. Using a dataset of 1,59,000 comments labelled across seven classes of toxicity, conventional machine learning and deep learning models are benchmarked across performance metrics. The study aims to quantify algorithmic capabilities to accurately classify bullying comments. The study finds that Support Vectors with a linear kernel surpass Logistic Regression in accurately identifying toxic comments. For deep learning techniques, the transformer models (BERT and Distil-BERT) deliver the highest performance among neural network architectures tested. The empirical evaluation provides insights into leveraging computational linguistics for automating the detection of online bullying at scale.

articleTitle: Scaling Up Video-to-Audio Conversion: A High-Performance Architecture Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: The vast array of programming techniques for audio and video files, large volumes of data, and different other essential components are all demonstrated by the quickly developing industry of audio and video publication. The digital publication company found it incredibly difficult to swiftly and effectively convert to a single coding format when faced with vast and varied data. This research suggests a distributed online audio and video format change stage with a B/S structure in response to demand and the current circumstance. It is constructed using the open source and cost-free FFMPEG format conversion tool in conjunction with the development architecture of React, Python, and JavaScript. The effective audio and video format change system created in this work is develop on the Java programming language. Its "Front end display system," "core scheduling backend server," and "conversion backend server" are all built on Java. This paper presents a comprehensive study of the key technologies and design tenets utilised to develop platform architecture. The usage of a platform for batch audio and video format change may considerably increase the conversion effectiveness of audio and video files while lowering the difficulty of the process as compared to a standard audio and video conversion scheme. The central idea in this study has a number of real-world applications and has been successfully applied to the processing of huge file batches. The process of extracting audio from a video clip and saving it as a distinct audio file is known as video to audio conversion. People prefer to listen to audio content on the go, which is driving up demand for video to audio conversion in today's multimedia world. Technology improvements have made it feasible to convert video to audio more quickly and effectively while maintaining the audio's quality. Users may easily and quickly extract audio from videos, thanks to the speedy conversion process, so they can listen to their preferred podcasts, music, or other audio content on their portable devices without having to view the entire film

articleTitle: Gray Level Image Contrast Enhancement Using Hybrid BAT and Moth Flame Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: This study presents a novel hybrid method that optimizes contrast stretching parameters for image enhancement by combining the Bat algorithm (BA) and Moth Flame Optimization (MFO). The method described in this study leverages the exploratory capabilities of the BA and the exploitation strengths of MFO in order to achieve an optimal balance between exploration and exploitation. The BA employs echolocation-inspired movements and randomization factors to explore the search space, while the MFO exploits locally optimal solutions guided by light sources. By integrating BA and MFO, the algorithm achieves a balance between exploration and exploitation, leading to improved solution quality and faster convergence. The algorithm iteratively moves the bats and moths, applies contrast stretching using updated positions, and evaluates the fitness value. The best solutions are identified and stored throughout the iterations. The algorithm extracts the optimal contrast stretching parameters from the best solution and applies them to enhance the input image. The experimental results demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness in improving image quality by 7.5 % and 24.2% with respect to BA and MFO. Thus the proposed hybrid algorithm offers a promising approach for image enhancement for various applications.

articleTitle: Skin Cancer Classification using ConvNET
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: “Face is the Index of Mind” is what they say, and so is the case with “Skin is the Index of Body”. No matter what the complexion of the person is, no matter what region of the globe they belong to, humans have always had skin, and with that comes the issue of skin imperfections and skin diseases. In this generation where even a small blemish can lead to a lot of insecurities in a person, these are to be answered with a lot of precision and trust. This model is our idea of addressing the issue, when the subject being dealt here is Skin Cancer, the stakes are even higher and the chances to go wrong are extremely thin. Hence came the novel idea of developing this model. Since skin cancer is a serious issue that affects people of all skin types and regions. Our model aims to provide answers to major skin cancer types at the user’s fingertips. We have developed a machine learning model that uses a basic Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to classify skin cancer images with high precision. The CNN model works by picking up patterns and details from images very effectively, just like how a human mind works. Our model has an accuracy of 71.03% in detecting skin cancer types. Our model is highly efficient and useful, and it stands tall on the pillars of pattern recognition and detail extraction from images.

articleTitle: Modern Systems and Algorithms for Enhanced Personal Well-being Data Management
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: In this era of pervasive connection and data collecting, it is more important than ever that people have access to and control over their own health data. This presentation offers a comprehensive overview of the most recent techniques and algorithms for the expedited processing of health-related data. Individuals may now gather and track an unprecedented amount of data about their health and fitness thanks to wearable devices, smartphone applications, and Internet of Things (IoT) sensors. The potential benefits of better health outcomes, accelerated research, and patient empowerment may be enormous if this data could be managed correctly. This article digs into the innovative programs and algorithms that are changing the face of current healthcare data management. First, we examine the scalability, security, and interoperability of current data storage and retrieval techniques in detail. Some examples of information that might be collected, saved, and accessed with the use of such devices include physiological measurements, data on lifestyle choices, and medical records. This abstract also investigates potential future applications of innovative data processing and analysis techniques for gathering data on the health of the general public. Innovative methods for health data management, such as blockchain and federated learning, are discussed in depth in the abstract. By facilitating the safe and transparent exchange of data between academics, healthcare providers, and patients, technology developments like these foster collaboration and accelerate medical research. The study emphasizes the significance of users having control over and ownership of their data in health data management. Customizable dashboards, mobile applications, and user interfaces that are made as simple as possible allow people to actively engage with their own health data and make informed decisions. The vast potential of the health data landscape may be tapped with the help of state-of-the-art technology infrastructures and algorithms. Realizing this potential can revolutionize health care and offer individuals more control over their own care.

articleTitle: Ensemble Neural Network Based Fish Species Identification for Emerging Aquaculture Application
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: Precision fish farming is a novel idea in the aquaculture research and development industry that integrates modern technology and pre-data processing methodologies inorder to allow data-driven decisions in precise fish farming. The objectives are to use contactless technologies to automate the process of monitoring fish, improve infrastructure, and marine environment. Individualized treatment, biomass measurement, and fish status assessment all depend on the ability to identify specific fish of same species within group frame. Recent studies have demonstrated that specific fish body patterns are used for individual species identification, but there is currently no system for automation of this process. We here have introduced a method to entirely automate identification of the fish species entirely based on their characteristics. Therefore, we adopted Ensemble of MobileNetV3 and NASNets, also known as (Ens_MobV3+NasNet), to excusively automate the process of classification of the species present in the Deep Vision trawl camera system images. Speeded-up robust features, which are based on realistic simulations of the Deep Vision images, are used to increase speed. Fish4Knowledge dataset is used for study, and it is discovered that the suggested Ens_MobV3+NasNet achieves 98.0% accuracy, 95% precision, 94.3% recall, and 91% F1-score.

articleTitle: Enhancing Boiler-Turbine Trajectory Tracking with LQR-Optimized PID Control Strategy
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Recent Advances in Science and Engineering Technology (ICRASET)
abstract: The goal of this research is to stabilize and track the trajectory for electrical power produced by a boiler turbine system utilizing a Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller. The controller gains are computed using a linear quadratic regulator (LQR). Initially, the system's nonlinear mathematical model is derived from the first principle model. The nonlinear system is subsequently linearized around the equilibrium point by using the Taylor series to create the stabilizing controller. Finally, the LQR theory is used to calculate the gains of the PID controller to obtain the required response for the electrical power. In this paper, a criteria for choosing the weighting matrices of LQR for tracking electrical power is provided, based on the damping ratio and natural frequency of the closed loop system. The performance of the boiler turbine system is analyzed on the generated electrical power output generated. The results show that the suggested control approach is successful in rejecting disturbances present in the system as well as stabilizing the electrical power of the boiler turbine system. The analysis of the controller’s performance is conducted through the calculation of Integral absolute error (IAE), Integral square error (ISE), and Integral time absolute error (ITAE) which gives insights into the controller’s effectiveness in regulating the system behavior.
